agents.name: Academic Curriculum Agent
agents.description: Acts as the single authoritative source for curriculum structure across all programmes and regulations. Every other academic agent depends on it to know what a course is, which semester it belongs to, how many credits it carries, and which regulation batch it applies to. Getting this agent right first removes ambiguity from the entire platform.
agents.primary_users: Heads of Department, Deans, Controller of Examinations, Board of Studies members, faculty, students.
agents.inputs: Approved curriculum and syllabus documents, Board of Studies resolutions, regulation books, credit structure tables, course category classifications, and the programme-wise course catalogue.
agents.outputs: Programme structure sheets, semester-wise course lists, credit distribution summaries, prerequisite maps, category-wise credit compliance reports against AICTE and university norms. Integrations. Feeds Agents 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 31, and 54. Design note. Treat regulation versioning as a first-class requirement, not an afterthought. An institution typically has three or four active regulation versions running simultaneously across batches, and confusing them is the most frequent source of wrong answers in academic systems.

agents.inputs: Syllabus documents at unit and topic granularity, textbook and reference book lists, Course Outcome statements, and the CO-PO-PSO mapping matrix.
agents.outputs: Unit-wise content listings, course summary sheets, prerequisite chains, CO and PO mapping tables, textbook lists. Example query. “Give me the course contents of Data Structures for II B.Tech CSE under R23 regulation.” Integrations. Consumes Agent 1. Feeds Agents 5, 31, 32, and 67.

agents.name: Faculty Course Allocation Agent

agents.name: Timetable Agent
agents.description: Generates conflict-free timetables across sections, faculty, rooms, and laboratories, and regenerates them quickly when circumstances change. Manual timetabling absorbs weeks of senior faculty time every semester and still produces clashes discovered in week one.
agents.primary_users: Timetable coordinators, Heads of Department, faculty, students.
agents.inputs: Approved course allocation from Agent 3, section strength, room and laboratory inventory with capacity and equipment, working day and period structure, laboratory batch splits, faculty unavailability constraints, and institutional rules such as no more than three consecutive theory periods.
agents.outputs: Section, faculty, room, and laboratory timetables, clash reports, room utilisation statistics, faculty load distribution charts, substitution schedules. Integrations. Consumes Agents 1 and 3. Feeds Agents 5, 6, 30, and 61. Design note. Timetabling is computationally hard and is best solved with a dedicated constraint solver rather than a language model. The agent’s role is to gather constraints in natural language, invoke the solver, and explain the result. Do not ask a language model to place periods on a grid directly.

agents.name: Student Academic Risk Agent
agents.description: Produces a forward-looking risk assessment for each student across several distinct risk types, so that intervention happens before the risk materialises rather than after.
agents.primary_users: Mentors, Heads of Department, Deans, counselling cell, examination section.

agents.name: Student Performance Prediction Agent
agents.description: Forecasts likely academic outcomes early enough in the semester that the forecast can be falsified by action. A prediction delivered in week four is useful; the same prediction in week fifteen is only a summary.
agents.primary_users: Faculty, mentors, students, Heads of Department.
agents.inputs: Current semester internal assessment marks and attendance, historical relationships between internal and external performance for the same course, prior semester Grade Point Average, assignment and quiz data, and course difficulty history.
agents.outputs: Individual outcome projections with confidence ranges, counterfactual scenarios, section-level pass percentage forecasts, prediction accuracy reports. Integrations. Consumes Agents 7, 11, 33. Feeds Agents 14, 16, 69, 70. Guardrail. How a prediction is worded to a student matters more than its accuracy. “You are predicted to fail” is harmful and often self-fulfilling. “At your current attendance and internal marks, reaching a pass requires roughly this score in the end-semester examination, and here is what would make that comfortable” conveys the same information as an actionable target. Constrain the agent’s output templates accordingly.

agents.description: Answers prospective student and parent questions accurately and instantly, at any hour, in the enquirer’s preferred language. Admission enquiry volume is highly seasonal and concentrated, and the quality of the first response materially affects conversion.
agents.primary_users: Prospective students and parents, admission office staff, counsellors.

Constrain the agent to answer strictly from the curated knowledge base, never from model general knowledge, and never to state placement figures, fee amounts, or eligibility rules that are not present in an approved source.
